The fixtures' declared reference tariff; not any grid company's published tariff.

calibration.note: Aggregates of an anonymised office's meters (NO1, 2026-02-16..2026-10-27), published with the owner's consent. No address, owner or meter-point identifier. The hourly export itself is not in the repository.

assumptions: the heat pump's output is a share of the design heat load, not the installed radiator capacity
design heat load from transmission UA and ventilation with heat recovery at the certificate's setpoint and the design outdoor temperature; no infiltration term beyond what UA carries
the backup heater is the rest of the design load (the certificate's direct-electric share)
a ground-source pump: constant source temperature, no outdoor derating, no defrost
the Carnot fraction reproduces the certificate's seasonal COP at the stated mean supply
buffer volume by litres per kW; the site's actual tank replaces it
none of these is measured; the pilot's phase 0 verifies each against the plant's documentation

certificate.heat_source_note: ground-source heat pump with energy wells

open_questions: The certificate states 295 MWh measured electricity a year (2021); E01+E02 annualise to about 170 MWh in 2026: other main meters, or a real reduction?
Heating signature: certificate envelope gives 2345 W/K, the heat meters 1549 W/K (sparse in summer; 13 % of heat is direct electric).

tariff_in_runs.name: ASSUMPTION (D-13): a generic reference business tariff with an energy part and a power part on the month's highest hourly mean kW; not any grid company's published tariff. Taxes (elavgift, Enova fee, VAT) are excluded.

scope.method: IPMVP Option D (calibrated simulation); calibration reported against ASHRAE Guideline 14 (monthly CV(RMSE) <= 15 %, |NMBE| <= 5 %; hourly <= 30 %, <= 10 %).
established: The twin, calibrated to the site's named meters, reproduces the site's monthly electricity within the Guideline 14 monthly criteria on the metered period (in-sample).
On that twin, the strategies' energy, cost, peak and comfort differences are deterministic and reproducible from the pinned inputs and seeds.
Every supervisory change of the caretaker is one governed tool call with a decision record; the validator's refusals and routes are counted.
not_established: A measured saving in the building. The calibration is in-sample (the fit period is the validation period), monthly only (the hourly criterion is not met), and on nine months of 2026 while the savings year is 2025.

The as-found control. P0 is the testbed's generic as-found sequence (fixed schedules, constant tank), not the site's documented sequence; the site's real baseline may already contain some of the levers.

The plant as sized: the heat pump's output, the backup heater, the buffer volume and the ground-source temperature are derived from the certificate and stated assumptions (calibration.plant_sizing), not measured; whether the real plant stages its backup heater as the twin does, and whether lighting can be controlled by presence and daylight, are site questions.
The grid tariff's power part: priced on a published sheet, transcribed by hand, excluding taxes and the reactive-power charge; the site's contract may differ.
Physical OT safety. No write path to a real plant exists (INV-12).
scope.pilot_next: A 90-day pilot replaces every item above with measurement: the site's own control sequence as P0, a held-out validation period, the meters as the measurement boundary, and the governed caretaker in shadow then controlled operation under the signed limits.
